## Summary

Implements issue #212: relation-definition ownership and protected system entry points, building on #211's normalized relation edge contract.

- `CreateRelationPropertyInput` now carries independent `owner`/`ownerProcess`/`locked` per side (source and `inverse`), with `ownerProcess` required exactly when `owner: 'system'`.
- New `SystemRelationWriteContext { ownerProcess }` gates `createRelationPropertyWithClient`, `createRelationWithClient`, `updateRelationWithClient`, `deleteRelationWithClient`. Only the property named by `relationPropertyId` authorizes an edge write; a public caller (no context) or a mismatched system context is rejected `owner_violation`.
- The public facade (`createRelationProperty`/`createRelation`/`updateRelation`/`deleteRelation`) never passes a context, so it can never touch an `owner: 'system'` relation property.
- Relation-property creation now applies `locked` only after both sides' schema/config is fully written, so `locked: true` never leaves an externally visible unlocked intermediate state.
- Migrated every internal relation writer (seeds, mail ingest/draft/send/attachments/folderDiscovery/imap-gmail-graph reconcilers/personLinkingActions, `tasks/advanceTaskRecurrence`) onto the protected entry points with their registered process identity.
- Added real-Postgres integration tests for public rejection, matching/mismatching `ownerProcess`, mixed-owner paired definitions, and atomic locked one-way/paired creation.

Verified in this session: full monorepo build clean, unit tests 83/83 passing, integration tests 403/403 passing (real ephemeral Postgres).

## Summary

Pushed the code-review fixes commit addressing all findings from CI check "code-review" on PR #317:

- **Medium finding**: documented the per-side `locked` semantics on `CreateRelationPropertyInput` (locking is now independent per side; a caller must set `inverse.locked` explicitly to lock the paired property, whereas the old top-level `locked: true` used to cascade to both sides).
- **Low findings**: fixed `import/first` violations in `inboxStore.ts`/`inboxTickAction.ts`, corrected misaligned `deleteRelationWithClient(...)` call indentation in `gmailReconcile.ts`/`graphReconcile.ts`, reindented the nested `describe` block in `relations.test.ts`, and switched `mailboxClientView.test.ts`'s relation-writing test helpers to `withTransaction` for consistency.

Verified before pushing: clean `tsc --noEmit`, full monorepo build, 83/83 unit tests, and 403/403 integration tests (real ephemeral Postgres) all passing.

## Summary

Pushed the code-review fix commit addressing the remaining medium and low findings from CI check "code-review" on PR #317:

- **Medium finding**: `folders.mailbox`'s inverse (`mailboxes.folders`) and `emails.folder`'s inverse (`folders.emails`) had been left at the default `owner: 'user'`, letting a caller who knew the inverse property's id create/update/delete the same edge without any `EMAILS_MODULE_ID`/`FOLDERS_MODULE_ID` context — bypassing the ownership the source side declared. Both inverses are now explicitly `owner: 'system'` with the matching `ownerProcess`, closing the gap for both affected relations.
- **Low finding**: simplified `CreateRelationPropertyInput.inverse`'s type from a redundant `Omit<...> & Pick<...>` to plain `RelationPropertySideInput`.

Verified before pushing: clean `tsc --noEmit`, full monorepo build, 83/83 unit tests, and 403/403 integration tests (real ephemeral Postgres) all passing.
